note: The TzHaar Fight Cave. Everything a check here compares against, and where it came from.
monsters: the OSRS cache's own npc records, 3116-3128 - the six-value stats array read as
attack, defence, strength, hitpoints, ranged, magic. Two things confirm that order rather
than assuming it: TzTok-Jad's fourth value is 250, which is his hitpoints, and the wiki says
independently that his healers come at 150, which only means anything below 250; and every
size here matches the size the 377 art record already carried.
waves: an algorithm, not a table - thresholds 2^k-1, highest first, subtract and repeat. The
thirteen anchors are cells of the OSRS wiki's own wave table, and the battery generates all
62 waves from the enum's thresholds and checks them against these.
arena: measured off maps/m37_79.jm2 by flooding from the ENTRY tile, (44,61). Flooding from
the exit loc's own tile at (44,62) gives one more, because a flood counts its seed and that
tile is clipped by the loc standing on it - which is why the entry tile is one to its south.
the subset of those where a five-tile npc fits, which is what the spawn points are drawn from.
tokkul: the wiki gives the formula N*(N+1) and separately quotes 8032 for a full run. 63*64
plus the 4000 for Jad is exactly that, and the two agreeing is the only reason to trust either.
The eight cave npcs wear OSRS art now - models AND animations - and they are the same eight
records: stats, params, hunt modes and every script that hangs off them are untouched.
osrs/skeleton/models: what each record points at now.
art: ambient, contrast, size and the two resizes as the OSRS CACHE states them - which is also
exactly what the 377 records already carried, all eight of them, every field. Nothing here
moved, and the check is that nothing moved.
stated_by_record: ready and walk are in the cache record itself, so those two are read rather
than inferred. Everything else had to be paired.
anims: {field: [osrs seq, the 377 seq it replaces]}. THE PAIRING IS DERIVED, NOT REMEMBERED:
within a family the 377 set and the OSRS set hold the same animations at the same frame
counts, and (frames, priority) is unique per family, so each 377 seq has exactly one OSRS
partner. The battery re-derives it from all.seq and fightcave.seq every run.
jad_priority_exception: five families' priorities carry across unchanged. TzTok-Jad's three
attacks do not - 377 gives them 6 and OSRS gives them 10 - so for him the frame counts alone
separate them (12, 14, 31, all distinct), and all three were rendered on his own mesh.
Not one of the nine imported meshes has a single textured face, so every colour crossed over
exactly. The Infernal cape is the exception, and it is in "exchange" below.
The Fire cape exchange: TzHaar-Mej-Jal takes one Fire cape and rolls a ladder.
rates: CHOSEN, not sourced. There is nothing here to source them from - the exchange is not an
Old School mechanic, because there the Infernal cape comes from the Inferno and the Inferno
is in no cache here. The only rule they obey is the shape that was asked for: the cape
rarest, the two pets equal in the middle, Tokkul when nothing lands.
infernal: OSRS obj 21295. The twelve bonuses are the cache params, and the param ids are
proved by the Fire cape: OSRS obj 6570 carries {0-4: 1, 5-9: 11, 10: 4, 11: 2} and all.obj
already names those same twelve numbers on [tzhaar_cape_fire], so 0-4 are the attacks, 5-9
the defences, 10 strength and 11 prayer.
lava: 30 of the cape's 433 faces are textured in OSRS with texture 59 at colour 127 - white,
meaning untinted - and they wear that texture now. It is imported as LOCAL TEXTURE 50:
content/textures/lavacrust.png, OSRS sprite 318, black crust with molten cracks, animated
in direction 1 at speed 1. Three things had to move together for it - the image plus a
texture.pack line here, Pix3D.TEXTURE_COUNT in the Java client (50 slots to 128, because a
377 model names its texture by id in the face colour field and there was no id to give
it), and osrs2ob2.LOCAL_TEXTURES so the next import of anything using it keeps it too.
The Fight Cave art round shipped a substitution instead - 377's texture 40, the Fire
cape's own lava - because gentexhsl.py read the OSRS texture index BY POSITION, and that
index has 214 files whose ids run 0 to 214 with id 54 MISSING. Everything from 55 up was
off by one, so texture 59 was read as texture 60: jungle leaves, average colour HSL 12818,
an olive green. wrong_hsl is that colour, and the check that no face still carries it is
what pins the fix.
texture_pixels_sha1 is a hash of the DECODED pixels, not of the file: the bridge that
copies a file to the laptop re-encodes PNGs - same pixels, 5,770 more bytes - so a file
hash passes in the cloud and fails on the machine that matters.
jalrek: OSRS npc 10620 and obj 25519, the metamorphosis of TzRek-Jad. The cache also carries
5893 and 10625, second records with a "Metamorphosis" op, which is how Old School switches
between the two forms; here the exchange performs the change once and the pet stays changed.
